ICI rechallenge in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) involves the administration of immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) after a period of time following the initial treatment. The duration of the interval between the initial ICI treatment and rechallenge does not appear to affect the effectiveness of ICI rechallenge [F2, 64, 122, 123]. This suggests that the timing of rechallenge may not be a critical factor in determining the outcome of ICI therapy in HCC patients.
